incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: multiple containers restarting on node gpu-west-14 (SIGSEGV). Severity: P2. Paging oncall: liam

liam: i'm on. which pools and models are impacted? any customer-visible errors?

neha: us-west1-prod. we're seeing ~10% spike in 5xx for text-gen endpoints. Affected model images: redwood/pegasus-mini and redwood/pegasus-mini-int8. CrashLoopBackOff on pods bound to gpu-west-14.

sam: quick tail from pod runtime-pegasus-3a2c:
```
[2026-03-17T03:47:11Z] runtime_engine: cudaMalloc returned cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-17T03:47:11Z] runtime_engine: attempting recovery -> signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
  backtrace:
   runtime_engine() [0x7f4b1a...]
   trt_wrapper::Infer() [0x55d2f...]
   vllm::Scheduler::exec() [0x559b7...]
```

liam: neha, confirm node dmesg / nvml? looks like a device reset.

neha: dmesg: "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:af:00 has fallen off the bus" repeated and Xid 79 GPU reset entries at 03:47:10Z. gpu-watchdog logged a reset.

eng-sre: immediate plan proposal:
- cordon gpu-west-14, drain workloads to spare pools
- start a small canary fallback: redwood/pegasus-mini -> redwood/pegasus-mini-cpu-quant at 5%
- apply runtime safe-mode: reduce batch sizes, disable kv-cache for live sessions, and cap prefetch threads
- collect cores + nvml logs for RCA
Agree?

liam: agree. neha, cordon+drain now. sam, can you trigger the fallback canary and push safe-mode? jess, prep customer comms.

sam: doing canary now:
```
redwoodctl rollout create --from redwood/pegasus-mini --to redwood/pegasus-mini-cpu-quant --percent 5 --tag incident-20260317-pegasus
```
Canary started 03:55Z.

sam: pushing runtime safe-mode (max_batch 8->4, kv_cache=false, prefetch_threads 4->2):
```
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/models/redwood/pegasus-mini/config \\
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\
 -d '{"max_batch_size":4,"kv_cache":false,"prefetch_threads":2}'
```
Applied 03:56Z. Should roll within ~20s.

neha: cordon & taint applied: `kubectl cordon gpu-west-14 && kubectl taint nodes gpu-west-14 incident=evacuate:NoSchedule`. Draining: `kubectl drain gpu-west-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 1: pods moving to gpu-spare-1/2.

jess: drafted initial customer notice: "We
re investigating increased errors for certain text-generation endpoints in us-west1. Engineers are mitigating by routing traffic to fallback hosts; updates every 20 minutes." Ready to send once we confirm impacted count.

neha: observing restart rate drop after profile change on healthy nodes. gpu-west-14 still shows hardware resets during eviction.

sam: collecting artifacts from a crashed container runtime-pegasus-3a2c:
```
kubectl exec -it runtime-pegasus-3a2c -- bash -lc 'tar czf /tmp/collect.tgz /var/crash/core.* /var/log/runtime /var/log/nvidia /tmp/nvml_dump.log'
kubectl cp runtime-pegasus-3a2c:/tmp/collect.tgz ./pegasus-core-3a2c.tgz
aws s3 cp ./pegasus-core-3a2c.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-17/pegasus-core-3a2c.tgz
```
Upload complete.

eng-sre: also request node-level artifacts: /var/log/kern.log, dmesg, and output of `nvidia-smi -q` from the host. infra-hw to assist.

infra-hw: acknowledged. running vendor diagnostics and will pull `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and run memory-bist tests. ETA initial results 40m.

liam: sam, any quick runtime guard we can add to avoid deref after driver reset? e.g., add null checks around allocator free path or catch cuda errors earlier? If quick patch not possible, keep fallback and safe-mode until we have stability.

sam: quick defensive tweak rolled to the runtime image in the cluster: added guard to allocator free path and a retry on cudaMalloc with short backoff. Pushed as emergency container image `runtime-engine:incident-20260317-safe` to the canary cohort at 04:02Z.

neha: after canary and safe runtime, observed further reduction in 5xx to ~1.5% and pod restarts decreased on spare pool. gpu-west-14 still flapping; kept cordoned.

jess: sent initial notices to 5 affected customers and updated statuspage: "Mitigations applied; routing to spare pool and fallback models. We'll update every 20 minutes." Posted 04:10Z.

sam: core analysis early notes: backtrace shows null pointer deref in allocator cleanup path triggered during asynchronous cuda driver reset (Xid 79). nvml dump shows GPU reset coincident with allocation failures. Artifacts in S3.

eng-sre: next ops:
- keep node cordoned and schedule hardware maintenance if infra-hw confirms ECC/firmware faults
- maintain fallback until errors <1% for 30m
- schedule postmortem and include timeline, backtraces, nvml/dmesg, k8s events, and customer impact

infra-hw: vendor diagnostics indicate non-zero ECC recovered and some parity errors on GPU 0. Planning to RMA the device if additional tests fail. Logs pushed to incident S3.

liam: assigning action owners: neha (node coordination + hw follow-up), sam (core/backtrace + runtime patch follow-up), jess (customer comms), eng-sre (postmortem lead). ETA initial RCA doc in 6 hours.

sam: also queued transient scale-up: +4 GPUs in spare pool to absorb traffic during evacuation.

neha: node remains tainted with `incident=evacuate:NoSchedule`. No new pods scheduled there.

liam: monitoring. once errors hold <1% and no restarts for 30m, we'll mark mitigated. If flapping continues after evacuation, we'll escalate to full host replacement.
